newsitem.title: RUSSIA: KAZAKH GOVERNMENT CLOSELY WATCHES GRAIN HARVEST.
newsitem.headline: KAZAKH GOVERNMENT CLOSELY WATCHES GRAIN HARVEST.

text.p: Kazakhstan has set up a special government commission to ensure that state grain reserves are properly filled, Itar-Tass news agency said on Thursday.

It said the new body was necessary because farmers owed the state 1.25 million tonnes of grain since 1994 as payment for state credits. It said farmers had "improperly expended" 150,000 tonnes of grain, but did not explain what had happened.

Tass said the government would monitor grain levels by checking supplies brought in to around 100 silos across the Central Asian state. Improper storage had in the past led to losses of 200,000 tonnes of wheat, it said.

Tass quoted unnamed government officials as saying the harvest could total just 12-13 million tonnes this year. Previous state forecasts have said output would reach 14 million tonnes. Farmers sowed about 17 million hectares this year.
Last year's harvest, ravaged by drought, officially weighed in at just 11.6 million tonnes, half the levels seen in the Soviet era.
Kazakhstan's grain harvest is crucial to regional supplies.
Kazakhstan and Ukraine are the former Soviet Union's largest grain exporters, delivering mainly to Russia.
But the vast country has seen its output decline steadily over the past five years and fall well below the 20 million tonnes and more it produced before the 1991 Soviet collapse.
